The constitutional validity of the Act was challenged in the High Court and the High Court held that the provisions of the Act, other than s.28, were measures of agrarian reform and were protected by Art.31A of the Constitution. However, s.28 was held to be violative of Art.14 of the Constitution. In 1964, the Constitution (17th Amendment) Act was passed, as a result of which the 1961 Act, including s.28, was included in the Ninth Schedule. The 1961 Act was amended by various Maharashtra Acts, namely Act of 1968, of 1968, of 1969 and of 1970. The constitutional validity of the 1961-Act as amended by the various Maharashtra Acts was again challenged but the High Court upheld the validity of the Act as amended on the ground that it was protected by Arts.1A and 31B of the Constitution.
